items.q: The number of surahs in the Qur'an.
The opening surah of the Qur'an.
The longest surah of the Qur'an.
The angel who brought the revelation to our Beloved Master ﷺ.
The month in which the Qur'an was first sent down.
The night better than a thousand months, in which the Qur'an was sent down.
The language in which the Qur'an was revealed.
The Qur'an is divided into this many juz' (parts).
The only surah that does not begin with the Basmalah.
The cave where the first revelation came to our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
The first word revealed, meaning "Read!".
The surah named after the mother of Prophet 'Isa ﵇.
The surah whose name means "The Cave".
The short surah our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said equals a third of the Qur'an (paraphrased).
The verse our Beloved Master ﷺ called the greatest verse of the Qur'an (paraphrased).
The surah that calls its own story "the best of stories" (meaning).
A person who has memorised the whole Qur'an.
The shortest surah of the Qur'an.
The last surah in the Mushaf.
The surah named after the Blessed Prophet ﵇ who was swallowed by a great fish.
The holy book revealed to our Beloved Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
The written copy of the Qur'an between two covers.
A chapter of the Qur'an.
The phrase "Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim" is called this.
The surah named after the cow.
The surah named after the family of 'Imran.
The surah named after women.
The surah named after the ant.
The surah named after the spider.
The surah named after our Master Ibrahim ﵇.
The surah named after our Master Nuh ﵇.
The surah named after the Romans.
The surah named after the light.
The surah named after the jinn.
The surah named after the pen.
The surah named after the dawn.
The surah that begins "Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind" (meaning).
The surah that begins "Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak" (meaning).
The surah that begins "When the help of Allah and the victory come" (meaning).
The surah that begins "We have given you al-Kawthar" (meaning).
The surah that begins "By time" (meaning).
Juz' 30 is popularly named after its first word.
The first surah of Juz' 'Amma.
The surah recited in every rak'ah of the prayer.
"Amin" said after al-Fatihah means this.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said the best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and this (paraphrased).
Reading the Qur'an with correct pronunciation rules is called this.
Explaining the meanings of the Qur'an is called this.
The Qur'an was sent down in stages over about 23 years; this whole process is called this.
The Qur'an says Allah has guaranteed to do this to it.
The number of verses in Surah al-Fatihah.
Each juz' is split into two of these, giving 60 in all.
Surahs revealed before the Hijrah are called this.
Surahs revealed after the Hijrah are called this.
The surah that has the Basmalah inside a verse, in the letter of our master Sulayman ﵇.
The surah named after the bee.
The last two surahs, recited for protection, are together called this.
The Companion who led the gathering of the Qur'an and was a chief scribe of revelation.

items.q: The caliph who had the Qur'an gathered into one volume after the Battle of Yamamah.
items.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Virtues of the Qur'an

items.q: The caliph who had standard copies of the Mushaf sent to the provinces.
items.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Virtues of the Qur'an

items.q: The Companion who urged our master Abu Bakr ﵁ to collect the Qur'an after many reciters fell at Yamamah.
items.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Virtues of the Qur'an

items.q: The surah that names our Beloved Prophet's ﷺ uncle who opposed Him ﷺ.
The surah named after the elephant army.
The surah named after the tribe of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
The surah whose name means "Victory", revealed on the way back from Hudaybiyyah.
The verse that says there is no compulsion in religion.
The number of years over which the Qur'an was revealed, roughly.
The number of times the name "Muhammad ﷺ" appears in the Qur'an.
The surah in which our master 'Isa ﵇ gives good news of a Messenger named Ahmad.
The second surah in the Mushaf.
The third surah in the Mushaf.
The fourth surah in the Mushaf.
The surah number of Surah Yasin.
The surah number of Surah al-Kahf.
The surah number of Surah al-Mulk.
The surah number of Surah al-Rahman.
The surah number of Surah Maryam.
The number of verses in Surah al-Ikhlas.
The number of verses in Surah Yasin, by the Kufan count.
The number of verses in Surah al-Kahf, by the Kufan count.
The number of verses in Surah al-Mulk.
Our Beloved Master ﷺ said a surah of thirty verses interceded for a man until he was forgiven (paraphrased).
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said whoever reads this surah on Friday has light between the two Fridays (paraphrased).
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said memorising the first ten verses of this surah protects from the Dajjal (paraphrased).
The surah in which the Qur'an says Allah taught the Qur'an and created man.
The surah describing three groups of people on the Day: the foremost, the right and the left.
The surah describing the Night of Power.
The surah describing the earthquake of the Last Day.
The surah that opens with the coming of the blind Companion 'Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum ﵁.
The surah that says our lady Maryam ﵍ was chosen above the women of the worlds.
The surah named after the "Groups" led to Paradise or to Hell.
The surah that mentions the splitting of the moon, a sign given to our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
The surah in which the Qur'an is said to be made easy for remembrance, repeated four times.
The surah named after the "Kneeling" nations on the Day.
The surah named after the "Smoke".
The surah named after the "Sand dunes".
The surah named after the "Private rooms" of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
The surah named after the "Clans" (Confederates).
The surah named after "Those who drag forth" (angels ﵈) (meaning).
The surah named after "Those ranged in rows" (meaning).
The number of verses in Surah al-Baqarah.
The number of surahs that begin with "Ha Mim".
The name for the separate letters at the start of some surahs, such as Alif Lam Mim.
The number of surahs that begin with separate letters.
The surah named after iron.
The surah that tells of the Table sent down for the disciples of our master 'Isa ﵇.
The surah that tells of the Sleepers of the Cave, Musa ﵇ with our master al-Khidr ﵇, and Dhul-Qarnayn.
The surah named after the Night Journey.
The surah whose opening verses were the first to be revealed.
The Blessed Prophet ﵇ named most often in the Qur'an.
The only woman named in the Qur'an.
The only Companion named in the Qur'an.
The surah that deals at length with the Battle of Badr.
The surah that tells of the Battle of the Trench.
The surah that cleared our lady 'A'ishah ﵂ of the slander.
The two surahs our Beloved Master ﷺ called al-Zahrawan, "the two bright ones" (meaning).
The surah in which a wise man advises his son.
The surah that opens with a woman pleading her case about her husband.
The surah beginning "Tabarak", recited at night by many for protection in the grave.
The Arabic word for a verse of the Qur'an, which also means "sign".
The surah of Juz' 'Amma that tells of the overwhelming event (al-Ghashiyah).
The surah that tells of the people of the ditch (Ashab al-Ukhdud).
The surah that tells of the people of 'Ad, Thamud and Fir'awn in Juz' 'Amma, with Iram of the pillars.
The surah that tells of the she-camel of our master Salih ﵇ in Juz' 'Amma.
The surah that warns those who give short measure.
The surah in which the baby girl buried alive is asked for what sin she was killed.
The surah that tells of the owners of a garden who planned to keep the poor out.
The surah named after a believing man of Fir'awn's people, also called Ghafir.
The surah also called "Fussilat" or "Ha Mim al-Sajdah".
The surah also called "al-Insan" or "al-Dahr".
The surah also called "al-Inshirah".
The surah also called "Bara'ah".
The surah also called "al-Lahab".
The surah that tells of the Queen of Saba' and the hoopoe.
The surah that tells of Qarun and his treasures.
The surah that tells of the people of Saba' and the bursting dam.
The surah that tells of Talut, Jalut and the young our master Dawud ﵇.
The surah that tells of the cow the Israelites were told to slaughter.
The surah that tells of Habil and Qabil (the two sons of Adam ﵇).
The surah that tells of our master Yunus ﵇ and the gourd plant.
The surah that tells of our master Ibrahim ﵇ being told to sacrifice his son.
The surah that tells of our master Ayyub ﵇ striking the ground with his foot.
The surah that has the "Verse of Light" (meaning).
The surah that has the verse "Today I have perfected your religion for you" (meaning).
The surah that has the verse "Allah and His angels send blessings on our Beloved Prophet ﷺ" (meaning).
The surah that has the verse saying our Beloved Master Muhammad ﷺ is "the Seal of the Prophets" ﵈ (meaning).
The surah that has the verse on hijab "draw their outer garments" (jalabib).
The surah that commands fasting in Ramadan.
The surah that describes the wudu step by step.
The surah that commands Hajj "for whoever is able" (meaning).
The surah that changed the qiblah to al-Masjid al-Haram.
When the scribes differed, our master 'Uthman ﵁ told them to write in the dialect of this tribe.

items.q: The Companion named first among the four from whom our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said to learn the Qur'an (paraphrased).
The Mother of the Believers who kept the compiled sheets of the Qur'an after our master 'Umar ﵁.
items.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Virtues of the Qur'an

items.q: The scholar who chose the seven famous readers, d. 324 AH / 936 CE.
The most widespread reading today is Hafs from this reader of Kufah.
The reading of Warsh, common in North and West Africa, comes from this reader of Madinah.
The number of mass-transmitted readings (qira'at) recognised by Ibn al-Jazari ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The term for verses that are clear in meaning, from Qur'an 3:7.
The term for verses that are open to more than one meaning, from Qur'an 3:7.
The surah that repeats "So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?" (meaning).
The surah named after our Beloved Prophet ﷺ Himself ﷺ.
The surah that sets out most of the shares of inheritance.
The surah that lists the eight kinds of people who may receive zakat.
The surah named after the Blessed Prophet ﵇ sent to the people of 'Ad.
The surah named after the rocky land where Thamud lived.
The surah whose name means "The Criterion", one of the names of the Qur'an.
The total number of verses in the Qur'an by the Kufan count.
The term for a later ruling that replaces an earlier one in the Qur'an.
The word "Qur'an" comes from a root meaning this.
The surah in which our Beloved Master ﷺ is told to say "I do not worship what you worship" (meaning).
The Companion who recited Surah al-Rahman openly at the Ka'bah and was beaten for it, by the seerah report.
The Companion our Beloved Prophet ﷺ praised for his voice, saying he was given a flute of the family of our master Dawud ﵇ (paraphrased).
The Companion whose recitation the angels ﵈ came down to hear like lamps in a cloud, by the hadith.
The surah Usayd ibn Hudayr ﵁ was reciting when the angels ﵈ came down to listen.
The Companion our Beloved Prophet ﷺ asked to recite to Him ﷺ, who wept at Qur'an 4:41.
The number of sajdah (prostration) places in the Mushaf most widely printed today.
The Hanafi school counts this many obligatory sajdahs of recitation.
A name for the opening surah, meaning "the Seven Oft-Repeated".
The surah of Juz' 'Amma with the most verses.
The name given to the long surahs at the start of the Mushaf.
The name given to surahs of about a hundred verses.
The name given to the short surahs from Qaf (or al-Hujurat) to the end.
The term for the reasons or occasions of revelation.
The famous book on occasions of revelation by al-Wahidi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The term for the readings beyond the ten, not recited in prayer.
The reader of Kufah among the seven whose two transmitters are Khalaf and Khallad ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ما.
The reader of Basrah among the seven.
The reader of Makkah among the seven.
The reader of Damascus among the seven.
The reader of Kufah among the seven who was also a great grammarian.
The two transmitters of Ibn Kathir ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The two transmitters of Abu 'Amr ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The reading of al-Duri from Abu 'Amr ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ما is still read in this country today.
The script style in which the 'Uthmani Mushaf is written, following the Companions' ⁨(رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمْ)⁩ spelling.
The three conditions for an accepted reading: sound chain, agreement with Arabic, and this.
The hadith that says the Qur'an was revealed in this many ahruf (modes).
The two Companions ⁨(رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا)⁩ whose dispute over Surah al-Furqan led to the hadith of the seven ahruf.
items.a: Our master 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and Hisham ibn Hakim ⁨(رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا)⁩

items.q: The Companion who brought news to our master 'Uthman ﵁ of differences in recitation among the armies.
Those armies were fighting in these regions.
The year in which our master 'Uthman ﵁ had the copies made, approximately.
The Companion who said "Every verse, I know where and about what it came down" (paraphrased).
The term for the Qur'an's verse endings, like rhymes.
The two transmitters of the reading of Nafi' ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The two transmitters of the reading of 'Asim ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The master of the readings who wrote al-Nashr and the poem al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, d. 833 AH / 1429 CE.
The famous poem on the seven readings by Imam al-Shatibi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ (d. 590 AH / 1194 CE).
The scholar of al-Andalus who wrote al-Taysir on the seven readings, d. 444 AH / 1053 CE.
The surah in which every verse contains the word "Allah".
The verse many regard as the last revealed, according to a report from Ibn 'Abbas ⁨(رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا)⁩.
The term for the inimitability of the Qur'an.
In Surah Hud, the deniers are challenged to bring this many surahs like it.
In Surah al-Baqarah, the deniers are challenged to bring this many surahs like it.
A name of Surah al-Fatihah meaning "Mother of the Book".
The surah also known as Surah Bani Isra'il.
The two surahs named after a single letter.
The term for the order of verses within each surah, fixed by our Beloved Master ﷺ by consensus.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said these verses suffice whoever recites them at night (paraphrased).
items.a: The last two verses of al-Baqarah

items.q: The Companion to whom our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said Allah had told Him ﷺ to recite Surah al-Bayyinah, and he wept.
The grammarian of Basrah credited with the first vowel dots in the Mushaf, d. 69 AH / 688 CE.
The scholar of Basrah credited with today's vowel signs (fathah, dammah, kasrah), 2nd century AH / 8th century CE.
items.a: al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩

items.q: The measured, unhurried recitation commanded in Surah al-Muzzammil.
The famous Mushaf printed in Madinah follows the reading of Hafs ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ and this count of verses.
The book by Abu 'Amr al-Dani ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ on verse-counting.
The great book of Qur'anic sciences by al-Suyuti ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The book of Qur'anic sciences by al-Zarkashi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The surah with the verse "By your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge" (meaning).
The surah that contains two verses of sajdah, by the Shafi'i and Hanbali count.
The sajdah in Surah Sad is counted as a sajdah of thankfulness, not recitation, in this school.
Our Beloved Master ﷺ prostrated in Surah al-Najm, and all present prostrated except this person.
items.a: An old man (who lifted dust to his forehead)

items.q: The surah that tells how a group of jinn listened to the Qur'an and believed.
The place where the jinn heard our Beloved Prophet ﷺ reciting, by the seerah.
The surah that mentions the "Two Easts and Two Wests" (meaning).
The surah that mentions two seas that meet with a barrier between them, and pearls and coral.
The surah that says the heavens and earth were joined, then split apart.
The surah that describes the stages of the embryo, from drop to clot to lump.
The surah in which our Beloved Prophet ﷺ is told "And warn your nearest kin" (meaning).
The surah in which the Qur'an is called "a guidance and a healing" for the believers.
The surah that says "We have not neglected anything in the Book" (meaning).
The surah in which our master Musa ﵇ says "My Lord, expand my chest" (meaning).
The surah that opens with "Ta Ha".
The surah that opens with "Ya Sin".
The surah that opens with "Ta Sin Mim", the first of three.
The surah that opens with "Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad".
The surah that opens with "Alif Lam Mim Sad".
The surah that opens with "Alif Lam Mim Ra".
The surah that opens with "Ha Mim 'Ayn Sin Qaf".
The longest of the separate-letter openings has this many letters.
The surah named after the "Heights" between Paradise and Hell.
The surah named after the "Consultation".
The surah named after "The Woman who Disputes" (meaning).
The surah named after "The Woman Tested" (meaning).
The surah named after "Mutual Loss and Gain" (meaning).
The surah named after "The Cattle".
The surah named after "The Spoils of war" (meaning).
The word said to mark the middle of the Qur'an by letters.
